messages:
sarah_support: FYI customer ACME (dedicated pool c-47) reporting a sudden spike in 429s and auth timeouts this morning. They say it started after a long-context batch run. :rotating_light:

jason_sre: Any quick indicators? autoscale events?

sarah_support: Their dashboard shows a burst of kv-evictions and a metric 'kvcache_fragmentation_pct' jumping from ~12% to 74% within 10m. Autoscaler didn't add GPUs. Ticket SUP-4321 opened with logs attached.

mike_runtime: tag me. Do we have heap/kv slab logs for c-47?

acme_infra: pasted snippet from their side (sanitized):

```
[2025-11-02T09:12:03Z] kvcache: evict key_prefix=usr:session len=5120 freed=8MB
[2025-11-02T09:12:04Z] kvcache: slab_alloc fail: 0x3ff: fragmentation=73% free_slab=1
[2025-11-02T09:12:04Z] request: id=abc123 status=429 reason=kv_cache_full latency=210ms
[2025-11-02T09:12:05Z] auth: token_verify timeout=1500ms upstream=dedicated-c47
```

jason_sre: looks like memory is free but unusable due to fragmentation -> slab allocator can't find contiguous chunk for long-context KV entries. That will cause evictions and big tail latencies.

mike_runtime: I see. Did autoscaler trigger on GPU utilization only? If so it might not have seen the KV memory pressure because we expose only host mem used, not fragmentation.

emily_pm: Customer says their requests are long-context ~30-40k tokens (embedding + context prep). Could be many large KV cache entries per session.

acme_infra: repro steps we ran: 1) open 120 concurrent sessions w/ ~35k token prefixes 2) stream repeated token appends 3) after ~6 minutes started seeing 429s and auth timeouts. We can reproduce on their dedicated pool.

jason_sre: thanks. Short-term mitigation: reduce tenant max_context or enable prefix coalescing to avoid creating massive KV blobs. Also can evict aggressively by LRU threshold.

mike_runtime: I'll patch the runtime to surface slab_fragmentation_pct and per-tenant kv_resident_slots as metrics, but that's not immediate. For an immediate workaround we can flip the per-tenant "spill_to_disk" option (experimental) so large KV pages get spilled to local SSD and avoid contiguous slab allocations. Any objections?

sarah_support: ACME agreed to try spill_to_disk, they asked for step-by-step.

mike_runtime: steps to enable (for Dedicated):
```
# on control plane for tenant acme
redwoodctl tenant update acme --kv-config '{"spill_to_disk":true,"max_kv_block":1MB}'
# restart serving worker on pool c-47
redwoodctl pool restart c-47 --graceful
```

acme_infra: applying now.

ops-bot: deployment acme-kv-spill started by mike_runtime at 2025-11-02T09:25:10Z

acme_infra: patch applied, pool restarted. Initial signs: evictions dropped and 429s decreased from 18% to ~2% over 5m.

jason_sre: good. Root cause summary for the incident doc: long-context workload created many large KV entries -> allocator fragmentation -> inability to satisfy contiguous allocation -> bulk evictions -> request failures. Autoscaler didn't trigger because fragmentation metric wasn't exported to policy.

emily_pm: action items?

mike_runtime: 1) expose slab_fragmentation_pct and per-tenant kv_slot_pressure (ENG-RUNTIME) 2) add autoscaler policy hook for kv_pressure to scale based on fragmentation or eviction_rate (ENG-INFRA) 3) add a safe default for Dedicated: enable spill_to_disk for tenants with average KV size > 512KB (PRODUCT) 4) docs + runbook for support (DEVEX)

jason_sre: I'll own the postmortem and timeline. Assigning to mike_runtime for metric + short-term runtime patch.

acme_infra: thanks for fast help, we can keep this as P1 until workaround is fully stable.

sarah_support: marking ticket SUP-4321 as escalated -> eng-runtime + eng-infra. Will follow up with timeline and PM notes. :white_check_mark:

mike_runtime: quick note for reproability: their repro load used a pattern that creates many small prefixes per session (user-generated tokens as prefix ids). If customers use a single stable prefix per session we see much lower fragmentation. Recommend we add guidance to best-practice docs.

emily_pm: noted. I'll add doc blurb and surface to onboarding.

jason_sre: last: schedule a short run with ACME team to validate post-fix. I'll coordinate times.

sarah_support: thanks all. Closing slack thread for now but will update SUP-4321 and the postmortem link here when ready.
